identity.description: Asana work management platform (Work Graph); developer docs at developers.asana.com cover its REST API, OAuth, webhooks, and MCP server.
identity.identity_notes: developers.asana.com documents Asana's own platform and API; the fetched overview calls the REST API 'the primary feature of Asana's platform'. Product matches the 'Asana' work-management app. I did not fetch the asana.com homepage.

auth.oauth_flows: Authorization code grant only (per docs); access tokens last one hour; refresh tokens issued. Client ID and secret come from an app registered in the developer console.
auth.token_refresh: Refresh token can be used to fetch a new access token when the current one expires (OAuth). PATs are long-lived and do not require refresh. Service accounts are described as long-lived tokens.
auth.scopes_notes: Scopes exist and must be registered in the developer console; only registered scopes are accepted during authorization. Apps may instead request 'Full permissions', which the docs say is not recommended. Service accounts have their own scope configuration.

access.production_restrictions: OAuth apps must be made available in a user's workspace to be authorized (distribution settings). Service-account creation is restricted to super admins. Whether public listing requires Asana review was not established. PATs can be created by any developer-console user for testing in any workspace they belong to or in a free account.

api.rate_limits: Limits are per authorization token, per minute: 150 requests/min on free domains and 1,500/min on paid domains; search API 60/min; GET concurrency 50, writes 15; 429 responses include Retry-After.
api.limitations: Webhooks on Workspace, Team, or Portfolio subscriptions do not support field filters. Java client is end-of-support; Ruby also end-of-support. Full endpoint list was not fetched; Broad rating rests on tasks, projects, portfolios, goals, and webhooks evidence plus the OpenAPI-generated reference.
